reviews.title: Divinity: Original Sin 2 review
reviews.author: Janine Hawkins
evidence: Larian has created a role-playing game where almost anything can happen — for better and worse
Divinity: Original Sin 2 is rich with possibilities. There are countless interactions to consider, to exploit, or to stumble into, and so far that’s been as exciting as it’s been
I often find myself thinking about the limits of the games I play. When a game offers me three paths and I’m keening for some ideal fourth, I tell myself
But I’m over 18 hours into Divinity: Original Sin 2 , and in that time I can’t say that I’ve thought about its limits once. Of course it has them,

From the very beginning Original Sin 2 feels wonderfully flexible. Players can customize their own characters (down to picking an instrument to highlight their personal soundtrack) or choose from several

Origin characters will become companions if they aren’t picked as the player character, meaning that their stories and the unique interactions they can have aren’t completely locked off. Better still,
It’s an RPG that is overwhelmingly about planning ahead yet still being completely taken by surprise
